reviewMethod: Complete line-by-line semantic review of five CI and staging-evidence workflows plus the structural CI workflow policy and its negative tests, including trigger and permission scope, exact-head checkout and artifact identity, action pinning, job time bounds, Node/npm runtime contracts, production environment fixtures, service dependencies, failure diagnostics, staging release ancestry and comment-spoof resistance.

residualRisks.statement: This bounded slice reviews seven CI-evidence files only; every other Batch 1 path retains its pending status and no repository-wide completion claim is made.

Diagnostic artifacts are now labeled with the exact checked-out source SHA, but most are troubleshooting logs rather than internally signed attestations and retain their bounded GitHub artifact retention periods.

The staging scheduler workflow now rejects releases older than the approved authority baseline, but no staging-host activation is claimed until the protected runner, environment, alert destination and accepted evidence required by issue #229 exist.

reviewNotes: Main and pull-request triggers, read-only permissions, concurrency, exact-head checkout, pinned actions, npm runtime enforcement, fail-preserving manifest execution, unconditional policy tests and failure-only diagnostics were reviewed.
The diagnostic artifact name now carries the exact checked-out pull-request head or push SHA rather than the pull-request synthetic merge SHA.

findings.attackPath: A pull-request diagnostic artifact was labeled with github.sha even though the workflow checked out github.event.pull_request.head.sha, causing evidence for one source tree to carry the identity of GitHub's synthetic merge commit.
findings.affectedInvariant: Every workflow artifact must be labeled with the exact source commit that produced its contents.
findings.evidence: The former artifact name used github.sha while checkout and verification used the pull-request head SHA; the remediated name uses the same head-or-push expression as checkout.
findings.verificationRequirement: The structural CI workflow policy must parse the effective upload step and reject github.sha-only or comment-spoofed artifact names.

reviewNotes: Both jobs, service images, environment contract, exact-head checkout, pinned actions, migrations, type and lint authorities, domain-specific guards, service-backed tests, full test suite, production build, runtime smokes and failure diagnostics were reviewed as the primary integration gate.

Hygiene and quality jobs now have explicit 10- and 60-minute bounds, all diagnostic artifacts use the exact source SHA, and the new structural CI workflow guard runs before the remaining security authorities.

Exact-head CI and Full Suite exposed destructive migration authority tests mutating the shared service database while unrelated notification and session suites were reading its ledger; every checksum-mutation case now uses a UUID-scoped database with bounded cleanup.

The Production environment contract now uses distinct non-placeholder CI fixtures accepted by the same fail-closed validator as runtime startup, and failure-only diagnostic uploads cannot add a second failure when an earlier step skipped their producer.

findings.attackPath: Every pull-request artifact emitted by the primary CI workflow used the synthetic merge SHA in its name while both jobs executed the exact pull-request head.
findings.affectedInvariant: Repository hygiene and failure diagnostics must be attributable to the exact source tree that produced them.
findings.evidence: The former hygiene and fourteen diagnostic artifact names used github.sha; all remediated names use github.event.pull_request.head.sha with the push SHA fallback.
findings.verificationRequirement: The structural policy must inspect every effective upload-artifact step and reject any name that lacks the exact governed evidence SHA.

findings.attackPath: A hung hygiene command, dependency install, service-backed test or production build could occupy the primary required CI job until GitHub's broad default job deadline.
findings.affectedInvariant: Every required CI job must fail within a deliberate bounded operational deadline.
findings.evidence: Neither CI job previously declared timeout-minutes; the remediated hygiene and quality jobs declare 10 and 60 minutes respectively.
findings.verificationRequirement: The structural policy must require the exact bounded timeout for every governed CI job and reject missing or expanded values.

findings.attackPath: The primary npm test step ran destructive migration-authority cases in parallel with other service-backed suites against one shared PostgreSQL database, allowing temporary checksum mutations to make unrelated notification or session tests fail nondeterministically.
findings.affectedInvariant: A required exact-head CI result must be determined by the tested source, not by cross-suite mutation order in a shared service fixture.
findings.evidence: CI run 30505060431 captured migration-concurrency checksum mutation racing notification outbox tests; Full Suite run 30514643759 later captured migration-integration compatibility-checksum mutation racing logout tests, which observed database_schema_not_ready:outdated. Both mutation paths now use UUID-scoped databases and bounded forced cleanup.
findings.verificationRequirement: The exact-head primary CI and Full Suite workflows must both pass the service-backed test suite with every migration checksum-mutation case confined to an isolated database.

findings.attackPath: The primary CI Production environment contract supplied required and optional values containing the validator's rejected placeholder marker, so the newly complete fail-closed validator stopped the job before migrations, TypeScript, lint, tests or build could run.
findings.affectedInvariant: The required CI production preflight must exercise a complete syntactically valid non-production fixture without weakening or bypassing the runtime validator.
findings.evidence: CI run 30513139519 on exact head 053e6221 failed in Production environment contract and reported the placeholder marker in ten configured secrets and URLs.
findings.verificationRequirement: The workflow fixture must use distinct non-placeholder test values, env:check must pass in production mode and the structural policy must reject any placeholder-bearing job environment value.

findings.attackPath: When Production environment validation stopped CI before ESLint, the failure-only ESLint artifact step required a file that its skipped producer never created and recorded an additional failed step.
findings.affectedInvariant: Conditional diagnostic collection must preserve the primary failure even when an earlier gate legitimately prevents the diagnostic producer from running.
findings.evidence: The same CI run reported No files were found for /tmp/tecpey-eslint-diagnostics.log after the Production environment contract failure.
findings.verificationRequirement: Every failure-only upload in the primary CI workflow must ignore an absent artifact, and the structural policy plus a negative mutation must reject regression to error.

reviewNotes: Pull-request trigger, read-only permissions, concurrency, job and test timeouts, digest-pinned PostgreSQL and Redis services, bounded test secrets, exact-head checkout, migrations, full-suite execution and always-uploaded diagnostics were reviewed.
The workflow now verifies npm 10 before installation and labels its artifact with the exact checked-out pull-request head.

findings.attackPath: The always-uploaded full-suite diagnostic log was named with the synthetic pull-request merge SHA rather than the exact head used for checkout and test execution.
findings.affectedInvariant: Full-suite evidence must be attributable to its exact tested source commit.
findings.evidence: The former upload name used github.sha; the remediated name uses the pull-request head expression.
findings.verificationRequirement: The structural CI workflow policy must reject an effective artifact name that does not include the exact evidence SHA.

findings.attackPath: The diagnostic workflow installed dependencies without verifying the repository's governed npm 10 engine contract, allowing runner image drift to change lockfile interpretation or install behavior.
findings.affectedInvariant: All governed Node CI workflows must execute with the declared npm major version.
findings.evidence: The workflow previously moved directly from setup-node to npm ci; it now verifies the npm major is exactly 10 before installation.
findings.verificationRequirement: The structural policy must require an effective npm version verification step in every governed workflow.

reviewNotes: Main and pull-request triggers, read-only permissions, retry-safe concurrency, job timeout, digest-pinned services, exact-head checkout, canonical migrations, withdrawal and retired-security guards, audit tests, TypeScript and failure diagnostics were reviewed.
Failure diagnostics now carry the exact source head identity used by checkout.

findings.attackPath: Sensitive-mutation diagnostics for a pull request were named with the synthetic merge SHA while the security job executed the exact pull-request head.
findings.affectedInvariant: Security diagnostics must identify the exact source commit whose authority was evaluated.
findings.evidence: The former upload name used github.sha; the remediated name uses the exact head-or-push SHA expression.
findings.verificationRequirement: The structural CI workflow policy must reject a sensitive-audit upload name that lacks the exact evidence SHA.

reviewNotes: Manual inputs, protected environment, non-cancelling serialization, self-hosted runner labels, exact release checkout, main ancestry, pinned actions, runtime identity, protected variables, collector, offline verifier, redacted summary and accepted artifact upload were reviewed.
The selected release must now be both an ancestor of current main and a descendant of the approved scheduler authority baseline.

findings.attackPath: An operator could select any historical ancestor of main, including a commit older than the approved scheduler evidence authority, and execute its collector code on the protected staging runner.
findings.affectedInvariant: Accepted staging evidence may only be collected by a main release at or after the approved minimum security baseline.
findings.evidence: The former verification checked only that release_sha was an ancestor of current main; the remediated step also proves the approved baseline is an ancestor of release_sha.
findings.verificationRequirement: The structural policy must parse the effective environment and command, bind the exact baseline SHA, and reject omission or comment-only presence of the lower-bound ancestry check.

reviewNotes: Comment handling, indentation, block boundaries, direct scalar maps, job and step extraction, exact permissions, timeouts, checkout identity, credential persistence, full-SHA action pins, artifact identity, Node/npm contracts, staging ancestry and aggregate failure reporting were reviewed.
The parser validates effective YAML nodes and strips comment-only controls; its contract is deliberately limited to the five declared workflows and rejects a missing or expanded source set.

Job-level environments are now parsed so the primary Production contract cannot reintroduce rejected placeholder values, and conditional failure uploads in that workflow must tolerate an absent file from a skipped producer.

The unchanged governed workflows and eight negative-test groups were reviewed, including synthetic merge identity, comment spoofing, missing and expanded deadlines, missing npm verification, rejected Production placeholders, secondary diagnostic failures, stale staging baseline, floating actions and permission expansion.
Fixtures assert their mutation precondition before policy evaluation so a source drift cannot turn a negative test into a silent no-op.
